requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects on node1.
requirements.summary: A root-owned sysctl policy sets accept_redirects to 0 for all, default, and wildcard interfaces. Direct checks showed all relevant live values at 0 before and after a reboot, including enp1s0 and lo.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 source-routed packets on node1.
requirements.summary: The persistent policy sets accept_source_route to 0 for all, default, and wildcard interfaces. Direct checks showed all relevant values remained 0 after reboot, including current interfaces.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using a solution compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: The solution used the platform-native sysctl mechanism without package installation. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were unchanged after execution and reboot; package health also remained clean.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. IPv4 redirect and source-route acceptance are disabled live and persistently across a directly observed reboot, while the installed RHEL release and kernel were preserved. The independent lifecycle snapshots corroborate the restart and healthy recovered state.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The only state-changing actions were creation/application of the required sysctl policy (cmd-5014e36259004050) and the mandatory bounded reboot (cmd-845c1a95621143ed); both directly supported required persistence or restart evidence. No failed services, unsafe new listeners, abandoned temporary files, or package damage were observed. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, acknowledged restart, a different post-restart identity, and recovered policy, services, networking, protected data, and node health.
